findings.reason: the section must either narrow the predicate to a rename onto an existing destination, or name `_reclaim_stale_node_dispatch_claim`'s semantic rename as a second retained exception in its text and done-when.
findings.text: §9's lifted predicate matches `os.replace`, `os.rename` and a one-argument `.replace`/`.rename` attribute call unconditionally, but `_reclaim_stale_node_dispatch_claim` performs `os.rename(path, stale)` at :1721 to move a dead holder's claim aside, which is a move-to-a-new-name and not a write-then-replace fork; the predicate therefore flags a third function and §9's head done-when ("the AST inventory test reports exactly two functions, the promoted primitive in reckon/_store.py and the directory rename in reckon/resources.py") is unsatisfiable as written, and §9 names only resources.py as a retained exception

findings.reason: the predicate must additionally match a module-parameter or aliased rename (or the section must drop obligation_snapshot from the base figure and state the instrument cannot see a rename passed as a parameter).
findings.text: the same predicate misses the fork §9 lists: `write_snapshot` calls `replace(str(staging), str(path))` where `replace` is a plain `Callable[[str, str], None` parameter (default `os.replace`) at :603, so `call_name` returns the bare name `replace`, not `os.replace`, and the predicate never fires; §9's base done-when ("run at the base revision the same test reports every site in the inventory above") cannot hold for `crew/obligation_snapshot.py`, so the fork is listed in the section but invisible to the instrument the section builds to find it

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §8 promotes one primitive (`_write_through_sibling_temporary`) that hides temp naming, mode, byte-fsync, rename and directory-fsync behind a single render-callback call, and §9 adds one predicate function over `definitions`; both hide more than they expose.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §8 extends the owner (`_store.py`) rather than adding beside it, and §9 reuses `interface_counts.read_trees`/`definitions` rather than walking the tree again; the declined `clones.functions_in` is correctly declined (its `_Function` holds only token windows, no call — verified at reckon/clones.py:149-169), and the frozen census is unimportable from the package.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 and §9 each add exactly one `public_definitions` (the promoted primitive; the ported inventory rule) and each states in its own text that the retired helpers are underscore-private and uncounted, so nothing can shrink and no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family is added; §7 adds none.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searches the codebase thoroughly and cites the real owners (`reckon/_store.py:_write_through_sibling_temporary`, the census `primitive_concepts`, `interface_counts.read_trees`/`definitions`), but the AST inventory it builds in §9 as its reuse map cannot detect every fork the section itself lists and flags a rename that is not a fork.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §8 keeps `write_json_atomically` as a thin JSON adapter but states why the promoted primitive is needed beyond it (line-log and HTML payloads the document-oriented adapter cannot express), so the second entry point is justified.
